tasks.title: Use native sign-in and offline mode
tasks.body:
# Use native sign-in and offline mode

The Android app offers **Continue with Google** and **Continue on this device**. Choose Google when you want the account's existing cloud diary; choose device mode to keep a diary without signing in. The first explicit Google login may open its consent screen. Later app launches restore the saved session instead of automatically starting browser authentication.

If you have an older Saapadu installation, keep it until you have checked the restored history. The new package has its own device storage. A JSON backup is the transfer path for an unsynced diary; simply installing another package does not copy the old application's preferences.

Native session storage and ordinary diary storage are separate. A network outage does not mean the locally saved diary has been erased. Do not clear app data as a first response to a temporary cloud error.

tasks.title: Edit body measurements and routine
tasks.body:
# Edit body measurements and routine

Open **More**, find your profile card, and choose **Edit**. The form includes name, current weight, height, age, goal weight, usual activity and the body reference used by the calorie equation. Review all measurements before saving; the form uses kilograms and centimetres rather than guessing units from the number entered.

Changing current weight also creates or corrects today's weigh-in. To enter a reading from a previous date, use the dated check-in screen instead. Editing age updates the stored birth-year approximation; it does not collect a full date of birth.

Activity and daily movement credit affect the calculation path, so choose them to describe the intended routine. A saved measurement refreshes the current recommendation while past diary targets retain their snapshots. The result remains an estimate, not a measured metabolic test.

tasks.title: Record and correct dated weight check-ins
tasks.body:
# Record and correct dated weight check-ins

Open **Progress → Log weight** to record a measurement with a date. There is one reading per calendar date: saving another reading for that date corrects the entry instead of counting the same day twice. Use **View and edit weight check-ins** to revisit the history.

Backdated entries improve the timeline but do not replace the current weight with an older measurement. The latest dated reading remains the current measurement. Future-dated readings are rejected. Check the selected date before saving a correction, especially when copying measurements from another app.

The weekly prompt is shown inside Saapadu; it is not a scheduled Android notification. Sparse history can still be logged normally. A personal trend estimate needs enough dated evidence, so a first check-in does not instantly create an observed weekly rate.

tasks.title: Understand requested and estimated goal dates
tasks.body:
# Understand requested and estimated goal dates

The requested date records your intention. The estimated date describes what the current plan or recent check-ins imply. Keeping those values separate lets the estimate change without rewriting what you originally selected.

With limited history, Saapadu uses its calorie-plan estimate. Three recent readings spanning at least two weeks allow an observed trend. A plateau or movement away from the selected goal can leave that trend date unavailable; the app does not invent a finish date merely to fill the card.

Adding a slower week does not automatically increase the deficit to chase the original deadline. Edit the goal plan explicitly when your intention changes. Historical days keep their recorded target snapshots. This distinction is useful when comparing past diary decisions with a forecast that has since moved.

tasks.title: Find familiar foods and choose servings
tasks.body:
# Find familiar foods and choose servings

Use **Log food** on Today or **Add food** in a diary meal. Search checks both the food name and its aliases, which helps when a familiar dish has more than one spelling. Category filters narrow the current results; clear a filter if an expected item disappears.

Select the food to open its serving controls. Read the serving label before changing the multiplier: one serving is the catalog's described portion, not automatically one gram or one full recipe. The calorie and nutrient preview scales with the selected servings.

Check the meal and date before saving. Home-cooked recipes vary, so the catalog numbers are estimates. When the available entry describes a substantially different portion or preparation, a custom food can be clearer than repeatedly guessing an unexplained multiplier.

tasks.title: Create a reusable custom food
tasks.body:
# Create a reusable custom food

Open the food picker and choose **Custom food** or **Create custom food**. Enter a recognizable name, a serving label, serving grams and the calories and nutrients for that same serving. A clear label such as a measured portion is easier to reuse than an unexplained number.

Keep calories, protein, carbohydrates, fat and fibre on the same portion basis. Do not enter calories per serving alongside protein for an entire batch. When using a package label, first check which quantity its nutrition table describes.

Saving creates a reusable food entry; it does not by itself mean that you ate it. Select the saved item and log the intended portion to the intended meal. Custom foods are part of the diary's backup data, so include them when checking a restored backup on another device.

tasks.title: Keep daily wellness entries on the right day
tasks.body:
# Keep daily wellness entries on the right day

Today includes controls for water, sleep and steps. Check the displayed date before editing: the selected day determines which wellness record is read and updated. The diary's food totals and the wellness signals are related views of the same selected calendar day.

Enter a daily total rather than assuming every edit adds another amount. For example, copying a watch's current step total is different from adding that total again each time you reopen the tracker. Sleep is recorded in hours, and water uses the unit shown by the control.

Values typed here are manual diary entries. Optional Health Connect imports are covered by their own guide; a manual entry is not proof that a device reading was imported. Changing steps may affect credited activity when movement credit is enabled. It does not create a second workout record or import the watch's underlying exercise history.

## Implementation references

tasks.title: Understand movement credit without double counting
tasks.body:
# Understand movement credit without double counting

Activity can appear as steps, logged workouts or a watch's active-calorie total. Those sources can describe overlapping movement. Saapadu compares the estimates instead of simply adding all three together, then uses a conservative fraction as diary credit when daily movement credit is enabled.

The profile's fixed-activity mode and daily-credit mode have different calculation paths. Review the profile setting if a workout appears in the activity log but does not increase the food budget. A recorded workout and a credited calorie allowance are separate concepts.

Keep watch entries to active calories rather than a whole-day total that includes resting energy. The activity screen labels its estimate accordingly. These calculations help explain the application's budget; they are not a direct measurement of energy use and should not be interpreted as permission to chase a device number.

tasks.title: Log workouts with duration and intensity
tasks.body:
# Log workouts with duration and intensity

Open **Activity → Log workout**, choose the activity and intensity, and set the duration. The preview estimates active energy using the chosen activity and the current profile measurement. Save only the session you intend to record for the selected day.

Similar activity names can have different intensity estimates. Review the full choice rather than selecting the first matching word. A longer duration should describe a longer session, not an adjustment made solely to reach a preferred calorie total.

After saving, review the session list and the daily totals. Watch active calories are entered separately. The budget applies its overlap rule, so recording a workout does not imply that its full estimated calories will be added again on top of steps and a watch total. Keep original device records if you need an independent history.

tasks.title: Use the fasting timer and preserve its history
tasks.body:
# Use the fasting timer and preserve its history

Open **Fasting** or the fasting shortcut in More. Choose a supported window before starting. Once a timer is active, end that window before selecting a different plan. The custom control uses the supported range rather than accepting an arbitrary duration.

Ending early is still a recorded event. Use **End & save** when you want the active window finished and retained in history. Leaving and reopening the screen is different from ending the timer; the start timestamp belongs to the saved fasting state.

Logging food remains possible. If a food contains calories, the picker offers an explicit choice about ending the fasting window instead of silently discarding the food entry. Read the app's consent and suitability prompts before starting. The timer is a diary tool and does not establish that a fasting routine is appropriate for a particular person.

tasks.title: Move a diary with a portable backup
tasks.body:
# Move a diary with a portable backup

Open **More → Data & backup → Copy backup** and save the complete JSON somewhere private. Keep the original text intact; copying only the profile section loses meals and other history. A backup is a separate recovery copy, not merely the visible screen.

On the destination installation, use **Restore** with the complete exported text. Keep the source app installed until you have checked the restored profile, meals, weights and other records. Different Android package identities do not share local preferences automatically.

Treat restore as an intentional replacement operation. Export the destination diary first if it already contains records you may want later. The cloud account and device backup paths serve different recovery needs, so a successful Google sign-in does not prove that an unsynced old device diary has been transferred.

tasks.title: Connect cloud history without losing an offline draft
tasks.body:
# Connect cloud history without losing an offline draft

A device diary and an existing signed-in diary can both contain valuable records. When first linking the device to an account with cloud history, Saapadu restores the cloud version and keeps the offline draft separately instead of deciding that the newest device timestamp should replace everything.

Use **Copy saved offline diary** in More to retrieve that retained draft. Keep both exports before manually combining or replacing histories. Copying the draft retrieves it; it is not an automatic record-by-record merge.

A failed ownership lookup must not upload the draft over an account whose history has not been read. Continue to protect the device copy while retrying the connection. On account changes, the previous owner's diary must not become the next account's upload. These boundaries are part of sync correctness, not just the visual sign-in screen.

tasks.title: Read diary dates and historical target snapshots
tasks.body:
# Read diary dates and historical target snapshots

The date selector determines which food, workout and wellness entries are displayed. Before editing a past meal, check the selected calendar day rather than assuming every screen has returned to today. A correct food on the wrong day can distort both daily totals.

Historical targets are snapshots. Later profile or weight changes refresh the current plan without retroactively changing what every older diary day showed. This makes it possible to interpret earlier records using the target that applied at the time.

A historical day's target and today's recommendation can therefore differ without indicating corruption. When investigating a difference, compare the selected date, saved wellness snapshot and current profile separately. Avoid deleting a day merely because its numbers do not equal today's recalculated estimate. Export a backup before performing broad recovery changes.

tasks.title: Read macros and next-meal prompts
tasks.body:
# Read macros and next-meal prompts

The Macros card displays eaten amounts against the selected day's goals for protein, carbohydrates, fat and fibre. These values are built from logged servings, so a missing meal or a mismatched serving basis affects the totals before any suggestion is considered.

Today also shows practical next-meal prompts and remaining nutrient gaps. Those prompts are simple application rules based on the current diary; they are not a personalized clinical meal plan or an automatically verified inventory of food available at home.

Start by correcting the diary if the result looks implausible. Review custom-food nutrient units and serving multipliers, then compare the selected date and current target settings. A suggestion can change after a meal is logged because its input totals changed. It does not mean the app changed the historical food's original nutrient values.

tasks.title: Navigate the night interface and verify layout changes
tasks.body:
# Navigate the night interface and verify layout changes

The main destinations are Today, Diary, Activity, Fasting, Progress and More. The phone uses bottom navigation; a wider layout uses a side rail. The home shell keeps the destinations in an indexed stack so changing tabs preserves their mounted screen state.

When checking a UI change, visit every destination rather than judging only the first screen. Repeat at narrow phone widths and with larger system text. Labels, form actions and the bottom navigation must remain usable without relying on colour alone.

The shared theme defines the night surfaces, foreground colours and typography. Prefer those semantic colours to hard-coded replacements in individual cards. Use the existing theme and profile widget checks when changing shared components. A visually clean desktop screenshot does not establish that a phone keyboard or enlarged text will fit.

tasks.title: Connect Health Connect for read-only imports
tasks.body:
# Connect Health Connect for read-only imports

On Android, open **More** and find the **Health Connect** card. It appears only when the device supports Health Connect. If the provider app is missing or needs an update, the card offers **Install Health Connect**; otherwise choose **Connect Health Connect** and review the permission screen. Saapadu asks only for read access to steps, active energy, exercise sessions, sleep, weight and body composition readings. You may allow just some of them; the app syncs whatever was granted.

A sync runs straight after access is granted, again when the app is opened or resumed, and whenever you press **Sync now**. Each sync reads the last 14 days, but never days before this diary first opened version 2.1, so older history keeps its original numbers. An automatic sync waits until the cloud diary has finished reconciling. The card shows the last sync time.

Saapadu never writes to Health Connect. **Stop syncing** ends future reads; values that were already imported stay in the diary. If a read fails, the card reports that the diary is unchanged, and you can try again later. Manage per-type permissions in the Health Connect settings rather than in Saapadu.

tasks.title: Understand how imported health data meets your own entries
tasks.body:
# Understand how imported health data meets your own entries

Health Connect values are stored beside your manual entries rather than over them. On Today, the steps and sleep tiles show your own total when it is above zero and the imported value otherwise; imported figures are labelled, for example **steps · imported**. Editing such a tile notes that your entry wins. Entering 0 for steps or sleep lets the imported value show again.

Imported weights are accepted only within a plausible range, and a weight you entered yourself on a date is never replaced. When the newest weight is imported, it also refreshes the profile's current weight. Imported exercise sessions appear in the activity list with **(Health Connect)** in the name. They cannot be deleted inside Saapadu; change them in Health Connect and the next sync replaces imported sessions in the window it read.

To avoid counting one session twice, imported workouts only count on a day that has no manual workouts; the list marks them as not counted otherwise. Movement credit still uses the largest single movement source rather than adding steps, workouts and watch calories together. All of these remain estimates.

tasks.title: Turn on meal and evening log reminders
tasks.body:
# Turn on meal and evening log reminders

Reminders are available in the Android app and are all off by default. While none are enabled, Today shows a one-time **Gentle reminders?** card. **Turn on** asks for notification permission and enables the breakfast, lunch and dinner reminders, the evening check and the weekly weigh-in. **Choose** opens the settings, and **Not now** hides the card. Later, use **More → Reminders**.

Each meal reminder is skipped once that meal has an entry for the day. The evening check only fires when the day looks incomplete: fewer than two of breakfast, lunch and dinner logged, or less than 40% of the calorie target. Turn a reminder on to see its time, then tap **Around HH:MM** to change it. Delivery is deliberately inexact to spare the battery, so expect a reminder near the chosen time rather than on the minute.

Reminders are planned a few days ahead and re-planned when the diary changes or the app opens. The settings belong to this phone and are not part of the diary backup. If Android blocks notifications for Saapadu, the app says so; allow them in Android settings.

tasks.title: Set weigh-in, fasting and supplement reminders
tasks.body:
# Set weigh-in, fasting and supplement reminders

Open **More → Reminders** for the remaining reminder types. **Weekly weigh-in** fires around the chosen time on the day your next weight check-in is due. If a check-in is already due, it fires today, or tomorrow when today's time has passed. When no tape measurement has been saved in the last two weeks, its message also suggests measuring waist, hip and chest.

**Fasting** has two parts. While no fasting window is running, it reminds you at the chosen start time. While a window is active, it sends a separate alert when the target time is reached; you still end and save the window yourself in the app. Reminders cannot tell whether you actually ate, so treat them as prompts, not records.

**Supplements** is a master switch. Each supplement keeps its own reminder time, set in its edit dialog, and a reminder is skipped once that supplement is ticked off for the day. Saving a supplement with its reminder turned on also turns the master switch on. If some supplements have reminders but the switch is off, the Supplements screen links back to Reminders.

tasks.title: Log again from recent and frequent foods
tasks.body:
# Log again from recent and frequent foods

Open the food picker with an empty search and the **All** category. Above the full list it shows **My combos**, then **Recent** and **Frequent**. Recent lists the foods you logged most recently, without repeats. Frequent lists foods logged at least twice in the last 60 days that are not already in Recent. Typing a search or choosing a category hides these sections.

Tapping a recent or frequent food opens the usual serving sheet, so check the quantity and meal before saving; the picker does not reuse the previous amount automatically.

From a diary meal's **⋮** menu you can also copy whole meals. **Copy yesterday's** meal adds the same foods and servings from the previous day. **Repeat last** meal finds the most recent earlier date with entries in that meal and asks for confirmation before adding them. Both add to the selected day. If a fast is running today and the copied foods contain calories, the app first asks whether to end the fast at this entry time or keep the timer. Copied entries are ordinary diary entries afterwards, so edit or delete any item that differs today.

tasks.title: Save a repeated meal as a combo
tasks.body:
# Save a repeated meal as a combo

Log a meal you eat often, then open that meal's **⋮** menu in the diary and choose **Save as combo**. The editor suggests a name such as "My usual breakfast", a usual meal, and each item with its servings. Adjust the servings, remove items that do not belong (at least one must remain), then press **Save combo**.

To use it, open the food picker with an empty search. **My combos** lists each combo with its item count, calories and protein; **Log** adds all its items in one step. The items go to the meal the picker was opened for, which may differ from the combo's usual meal. If a fast is running today and the combo has calories, you are asked whether to end the fast first.

Manage combos in **More → My combos**: tap one to edit it, or delete it. Deleting a combo does not change diary entries already logged from it. Combos are included in the diary backup. Their calorie figures are built from the saved items, so they remain estimates like any other food entry.

tasks.title: Track supplements and their daily tick-offs
tasks.body:
# Track supplements and their daily tick-offs

Use **Add** on the Today **Supplements** card, or **More → Supplements**. Give each item a name, an optional dose, a time slot (Morning, After workout or Night), and calories and protein per dose. Leave both at 0 for pills and vitamins. An optional reminder can be set in the same dialog.

Tick an item on Today to record it for the selected day; untick it to remove that record. A tick-off with calories or protein, such as a whey scoop, adds to that day's totals. If the same item, matched by name, is also logged as a food that day, it is counted only once and Today shows it as already in the food log. Each tick-off keeps the values it had when you ticked it, so editing a dose later does not rewrite earlier days.

The Supplements screen shows a streak and how many days this month an item was taken. Removing a supplement archives it, so past tick-offs keep their name. This is a personal log, not dosing advice; follow your clinician or the product label for what to take.

tasks.title: Read protein per meal and its dismissible tip
tasks.body:
# Read protein per meal and its dismissible tip

Each diary meal header shows that meal's calories and grams of protein, added up from its logged entries. Supplement tick-offs count toward the day's protein total but are not part of any single meal's figure.

For breakfast, lunch or dinner with at least one entry and less than about 20 g of protein, the meal card shows a short tip with the approximate gap and a few familiar additions, such as curd, dal, paneer, eggs or sundal. Snacks and empty meals do not get a tip. About 20 g is a simple rule of thumb used by the app, not a personal requirement, and the tip disappears once the meal's logged protein reaches it.

Press the close button to dismiss the tip. A dismissal applies only to that meal on that date, and dismissals older than about three weeks are dropped from this device. If a tip looks wrong, first check the serving amounts and the protein values of any custom foods in the meal. This per-meal tip is separate from the next-meal prompts on Today.

tasks.title: Understand the 4 L water default
tasks.body:
# Understand the 4 L water default

From the day this diary first opened version 2.1, each day counts 4000 ml of water unless you change it. Today marks such a day as **ml water (default)** and explains that it is counted as 4 L. The figure is an assumption for convenience, not a measurement, so adjust it only when you drank noticeably less or more.

The **−250**, **+250** and **+500** buttons adjust from the value shown, so pressing −250 on a default day records 3750 ml. Tapping the water tile asks for the day's total. Any edit, including an explicit 0, is kept for that day. **Reset to 4 L** appears on edited days and returns them to the default.

Days before that first 2.1 date show exactly what was stored, including 0, so earlier history is not reinterpreted. The start date is saved with the diary and its backup. Restoring a backup can move it earlier, never later. When checking a restored diary, compare a few days on both sides of that date before assuming water history changed.

tasks.title: Set a precise quantity with the serving editor
tasks.body:
# Set a precise quantity with the serving editor

The add-food sheet and diary entry edits share one quantity control. Drag the slider, or type into **Servings**, which accepts 0.1 to 10. When the food has a serving weight, a **Grams / ml** field appears as well. The two fields stay in sync: typing grams converts them to servings using the food's serving weight, and changing servings updates the grams.

Values are rounded to two decimal places and kept within the 0.1 to 10 range. Under the fields, the calories, protein, carbohydrates, fat and fibre update as you go, so you can check the total before saving. They are scaled from the food's per-serving values and are estimates.

To correct an amount already in the diary, tap the entry and use the same editor, then press **Save quantity**. Only the servings change; the food and meal stay the same. If the amount you ate is outside the range, or the serving weight does not match how you measure the food, a custom food with a clearer serving is easier to use than repeated large multipliers.

tasks.title: Add tape measurements and smart-scale readings
tasks.body:
# Add tape measurements and smart-scale readings

When saving a weight check-in, expand **Measurements & smart scale (optional)**. It holds waist, hip and chest, plus smart-scale fields such as body fat, muscle mass, bone mass, body water, visceral fat, BMR, metabolic age and lean body mass. Leave blank anything you do not track; clearing a field removes that value. A value that is not a positive number in range is flagged with **Check value**.

With Health Connect connected, matching readings can arrive automatically and are marked **Health Connect** under the field. Imports only fill empty fields or replace earlier imports. A value you type yourself for the same date replaces the imported one.

Progress shows a **Body measurements** card with the latest waist, hip, chest, body fat and muscle readings and their change across recent check-ins. It also notes when tape measurements are due; every two weeks is enough. Home scales vary with water and timing, so compare trends week to week. These readings do not change calorie targets.

tasks.body:
# Read the logging streak and weekly summary

Today shows a **logging streak** chip once you have one. It counts consecutive days with at least one food entry, ending today. If today has nothing logged yet, the streak still counts up to yesterday, so a morning check does not look broken. Water defaults, supplement tick-offs, weights and steps do not extend it; only food entries do.

Progress has a **This week** card covering the last seven days, including today. **Days logged** counts days with food entries. Average calories against the average target, and average protein, use logged days only, so a day you skipped is not read as zero intake. **Weight change** compares the latest reading in the week with the latest one before it, or with the first in the week, and shows a dash when there are not enough readings. Steps show a total and an average over days that have a step value, including imported ones.

The summary is calculated from the diary each time it is shown, so correcting an old entry updates it. Treat the averages as a rough weekly picture rather than a precise measure of intake.
